techniques.name: Phishing: Spearphishing Attachment
techniques.description: Adversaries may send spearphishing emails with malicious attachments to gain initial access to target systems. Attachments are typically weaponized Office documents or executable zips.
techniques.mitigation: Block executable attachments at the email gateway, enforce SPF/DKIM/DMARC, and use sandbox attachment scanning.
techniques.detection: Inspect incoming email logs for suspicious attachment extensions, anomalous file hashes, or macros executing PowerShell.

techniques.name: Command and Scripting Interpreter: PowerShell
techniques.description: Adversaries may use PowerShell to execute commands, scripts, or binaries. PowerShell provides interactive access and script execution capabilities.
techniques.mitigation: Configure PowerShell Constrained Language Mode, enable Script Block Logging (Event ID 4104), and restrict execution policies.
techniques.detection: Monitor process creation events (Event ID 4688 / Sysmon 1) for powershell.exe executing encoded commands (-EncodedCommand, -e, -nop).

techniques.name: Scheduled Task/Job: Scheduled Task
techniques.description: Adversaries may create scheduled tasks to execute programs at system startup or on a periodic schedule to maintain persistence.
techniques.mitigation: Limit administrative access, restrict schtasks.exe privileges, and monitor scheduled task creation.
techniques.detection: Monitor Windows Event ID 4698 (A scheduled task was created) and TaskScheduler operational logs.

techniques.name: Exploitation for Privilege Escalation
techniques.description: Adversaries may exploit software vulnerabilities to elevate access privileges, such as local kernel privilege escalation (e.g. CVE-2024-30080).
techniques.mitigation: Apply operating system security updates and vendor security patches promptly.
techniques.detection: Monitor for unexpected elevated token privileges, LSASS memory access, or system driver injection.

techniques.name: Remote Services: SMB/Windows Admin Shares
techniques.description: Adversaries may use SMB and Administrative Shares (C$, ADMIN$) to move laterally between hosts using stolen administrative credentials.
techniques.mitigation: Disable administrative shares if not required, isolate internal network segments, enforce SMB signing.
techniques.detection: Monitor Event ID 5140 (A network share object was accessed) and Event ID 4624 Type 3 network logons.

techniques.name: Exfiltration Over Web Service: Exfiltration to Cloud Storage
techniques.description: Adversaries may exfiltrate data to cloud storage services (e.g. AWS S3, Mega.nz, OneDrive) using legitimate client software or APIs.
techniques.mitigation: Enforce Data Loss Prevention (DLP) policies, restrict egress traffic to approved cloud storage domains, monitor AWS API access.
techniques.detection: Monitor outbound firewall logs, DNS requests to external cloud APIs, and CloudTrail PutObject / MultiPartUpload events.
